1. (Currently amended) A method of treating a brain, comprising: inserting an elongated device into the brain to create a path; radially expanding the device to create a working channel along the path; __radially reinforcing the device against the tissue to maintain the working channel__; and introducing a medical element into the working channel to perform a medical procedure on the brain.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the medical element is an instrument __and the device is removed after the medical procedure is completed__.

3. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the medical element is a medicament.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, further comprising creating an opening in a cranium, and inserting the elongated device through the opening __such that the device is positioned between tissue layers within the brain__.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the elongated device comprises a first radially expandable body surrounded by a stent, which is surrounded by a second radially expandable body.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, further comprising radially contracting and removing the device from the brain __after introducing the medical element and completing the medical procedure__.

7. (Currently amended) A method of treating a tissue, comprising: placing an elongated device into the tissue to create a path; radially expanding the device against the tissue to radially displace the tissue along the path; radially reinforcing the device against the tissue __by expanding an inner expandable body to expand a stent surrounding the inner expandable body__; and introducing a medical element through the device to perform a medical procedure on the tissue.

8. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, wherein the medical element is an instrument __and the device comprises a first radially expandable body surrounded by a stent, which is surrounded by a second radially expandable body__.

9. (Original) The method of claim 7, wherein the medical element is a medicament.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, further comprising inserting the elongated device between tissue layers __and removing the device after the medical procedure is completed__.

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, further comprising radially contracting and removing the device from the tissue __after the medical procedure is completed__.

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, further comprising treating the tissue in contact with the device with a haemostatic compound to reduce bleeding __during the creation of the working channel__.

13. (Original) A method of treating a tissue, comprising: placing an elongated device, having a first radially expandable body, surrounded by a stent, which is surrounded by a second radially expandable body, into the tissue to create a path; radially expanding the second expandable body against the tissue to radially displace the tissue along the path; radially expanding the first expandable body to radially expand the stent to reinforce the second expandable body against the tissue; radially contracting and removing the first expandable body to create a working channel through the stent; introducing a medical element through the channel to perform a medical procedure on the tissue; and radially contracting the second expandable body and removing the device from the tissue.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the medical element is an instrument __and the device is removed only after the medical procedure is completed and the working channel has been established__.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the medical element is a medicament __delivered through the working channel after the first expandable body has been removed__.

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, further comprising inserting the elongated device between tissue layers __within the brain__.

17. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, further comprising treating the tissue in contact with the device with a haemostatic compound to reduce bleeding __during the radial expansion of the second expandable body__.
